negative_findings.description: Neither Visa nor Mastercard publishes Ukraine-specific volume, card-count or interchange disclosure. Ukraine-level scheme figures found in the press are consistently attributed to the NBU, not to the schemes.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched in uk and en for Visa/Mastercard Ukraine results releases; only NBU-sourced share figures and generic marketing press surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Scheme-level UA numbers must be sourced from the regulator, not from scheme IR; do not expect an earnings-style series from the international schemes.

negative_findings.description: No published annual report or audited operational report for UPC, UkrCard, TAS Link or the EasyPay processing entity was located on the open web; volume claims ('400M+ transactions/year') come from company marketing pages and third-party profiles.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched in en and uk for processor annual reports/processing volumes; only marketing copy, LinkedIn/Crunchbase profiles and NBU designation notices found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Processing-volume estimates must be treated as vendor claims; audited numbers, if any, will only appear via SMIDA issuer filings for the PrJSC-form entities.

negative_findings.description: bank.gov.ua returned HTTP 403 on a direct statistics-page fetch, while its PDF assets and news pages are indexed and reachable in search results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single most important source for this cell is bot-defended; collection must use a browser-grade client. This is a hypothesis of bot protection, not evidence the site is down.

negative_findings.description: The NBU-designated important operator 'ТОВ ЕЙСІ ДІСКІ ПРОЦЕСІНГ' was not conclusively mapped to a public consumer brand/domain during this pass; the EasyPay association is an inference.
negative_findings.result_summary: Registry-derived legal name found, but no confirmed corporate site.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents mis-attribution of processing volumes to the wrong brand.

brief: For Ukraine's card-scheme and switching layer, the disclosure centre of gravity is the National Bank of Ukraine: it is simultaneously the regulator, the oversight body publishing card/POS/acquiring statistics, and the payment organisation behind the domestic PROSTIR scheme — so the NBU oversight report, quarterly digests, payments-market presentations and the payment-systems register carry essentially all the quantitative series, while prostir.gov.ua supplies participant-level detail and points onward to member banks. Visa and Mastercard publish no Ukraine-level results; their UA market-share figures circulating in the press are NBU-derived, making scheme IR a low-yield, context-only source. Non-bank processors and ATM network operators (UPC, UkrCard, TAS Link, and the EasyPay processing entity — the group the NBU designates as important payment infrastructure) disclose only marketing-grade volume claims, with audited numbers reachable only indirectly via SMIDA issuer filings and, for UPC, Raiffeisen Bank International group reporting. Main collection risk is technical rather than legal: bank.gov.ua returned 403 to a plain fetch and will need a browser-grade client, and several corporate URLs here remain unverified pending the liveness pass.
